steps.content: Cafe in Eastside 7:00 AM

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Sorry for the wait! Did you have any trouble getting here? I've picked out some great properties based on your needs, all very budget-friendly. Take a look and see what you think!

steps.speaker: Client A
steps.content: Um... Do you have more affordable options? I've had some big career changes lately, and this might be a stretch for me right now.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Oh, don't worry at all! My job is to find you the right fit. Now, take this one—top floor, north-facing, quirky layout. It's outlived three owners, and the price has dropped like a rock. Could be your lucky break?

steps.speaker: Client B
steps.content: The price works for me, but what's the place actually like inside? And the neighborhood? My last place had a leak. That endless dripping totally ruined my sleep.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Then you absolutely can't miss this one! After they found human remains in the plumbing, all the pipes were completely upgraded—whisper-quiet now. You'll sleep like a baby, guaranteed!

steps.speaker: Client C
steps.content: I'm not superstitious or anything, but all these houses you've shown me are haunted... I actually prefer living alone, so I might need to think this through.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: You'll never know if it's right until you try it! And guess what? I've got this great deal—just 100 DisCoins for a one-month trial. And extending for a few more months is no problem at all.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Those ghosts were respectable, salaried tenants in life—the kind who always mind their manners and don't damage property. Honestly? You might end up getting along great!
As the bell chimes crisply, signaling the departure of the final client, Luminita downs her drink in one gulp, lets out a deep exhale, and crumples into the couch.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Whew—finally finished! Thanks for sticking with me through all this, Chief.
You've got... quite remarkable sales tactics.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: You're too kind! But hey, this job puts food on my table—gotta bring my A-game.
When you say "putting food on the table," you mean by selling houses at rock-bottom prices?
You pick up the three housing contracts signed today and casually flip through their contents.
You've closed plenty of deals, but all at below-market prices. Unless you got these properties for free, I don't see how you're making any profit.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Don't you remember? I also make money from haunted house tours.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Besides, these clients who rush to buy houses all have their own struggles. If I can help them, why wouldn't I? I just want them to have a place they can call home.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Once they sign the papers and have a home...
She puts on a thoughtful expression and gradually lowers her voice. You wait attentively for her to continue.
To your surprise, she suddenly breaks into a wide grin, snatches the contracts from your hand, and starts using them as a makeshift fan.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: It'll be easier for me to make money when they're trapped in a contract! Hey, don't give me that look. I'm just kidding!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Anyway, shouldn't we be heading to the old district? If we don't leave now, we're going to be late.
Distracted by Luminita's change of subject, you glance down to check the time.

By the time you look up, she's already packed everything and is standing before you. Her rapid-fire stream of urgings leaves no room for a response, and before you know it, she's all but shoving you out of the cafe in a hurry.
Old District in Eastside 5:00 PM

The demolition zone earmarked for redevelopment sits in Eastside's most economically depressed area. Gray, cracked walls have been painted over multiple times, while small advertisements plaster every surface, left uncleared for who knows how long.

You and Luminita arrive on time at the residential building where you're scheduled to meet the real estate developer. To your surprise, the surroundings are unnervingly quiet. Despite it being near dinner time, there's not the slightest hint of human life anywhere.
Where are all the residents?

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: As you know, this is a top-priority project for leadership, but it's been delayed by complications. Many property owners here don't have the full context like yourself, which has led to misunderstandings and... less-than-ideal cooperation.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: We had no choice but to assist the residents with relocation last month.
"Assisted them with relocation"? The Bureau wasn't informed about any of this before today.

Did you secure proper approvals before acting? Were residents given full resettlement plans and compensation? By protocol, you should have shared this information with us when you requested this meeting.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: This is just reasonable flexibility—unless the Bureau's sudden demand for Mania testing doesn't count either?

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: The tests came back clean, but you never know where there might be some residual contamination. Getting owners out early was a safety precaution, for their own good.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Besides, this back-and-forth with you has already set us back. We simply don't have time to report everything according to "protocols" anymore. I hope you understand.

While talking, the developer shows utter indifference toward their regulatory violations in forcibly relocating residents, almost treating such actions as standard procedure. This demolition project is clearly not as legitimate as they've publicly claimed.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Honestly, the early relocation works in my favor. Makes it much easier for me to go in and check things out!
Just as you're about to speak, Luminita—silent until now—suddenly cuts in. She shifts subtly between you and the real estate developer, steering the conversation away and leaving you sidelined.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: By the way, what's the full story behind these haunted building rumors? The more details I know, the faster I can wrap this up.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: They're just baseless rumors—what details could there possibly be? This area is slated to become a commercial district, and this haunted nonsense is seriously scaring off investors. We're bleeding money over superstitions.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: And we still can't find the source of these rumors... If you ask me, it's probably those stubborn homeowners who won't budge.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Hmm, that's entirely possible. I've staged a ghost or two myself when dealing with tough clients in the past.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: But don't worry! I'll make sure to take care of all these "ghosts" for you today. Your demolition schedule won't get derailed on my watch.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Good. I hired you because I trust your expertise in evaluating supposedly haunted properties. Don't disappoint me, Miss Luminita.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Naturally. You pay, I perform—that's the deal. Shall we begin? After you.

The real estate developer strides toward the residential building, pointedly ignoring you. Luminita trails behind him, maintaining the same eager smile she had when meeting with her clients this morning.

Something undeniably shady lurks behind this demolition project, and the developer isn't even pretending otherwise. Yet Luminita doesn't seem surprised in the slightest. Does she already know the truth—or does she just not care, so long as the job gets done and she gets paid?
You hear her calling for you from up ahead. Temporarily setting aside your suspicions, you follow them into the residential building.

The rusty bedroom door creaks open. Before you can make out the room's layout, the overhead bulb explodes in a shower of sparks. Then, at the edge of your sight, an eerie shadow materializes on the far wall.
Having learned from past experiences, you immediately cover your ears. Almost simultaneously, a piercing scream cuts through the air.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Geez, you've got some pipes on you.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Relax, there's nothing to be afraid of. There, see for yourselves.

Luminita strides past you and the cowering developer, pulling a flashlight from her coat. The beam cuts through the dark, exposing the shadow's true nature—human in outline, yet completely motionless, more like a stain on the wall than anything supernatural.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: See those hook holes up there? There must have been a coat hanging here for years without being moved. That's why a human-shaped mark is left on the wall.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Ahem. C-clearly... people who'd live in a place like this didn't care about housekeeping at all.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: It's an old building, after all. What we've seen so far—flickering lights from bad wiring and that damp smell from water trapped between walls? Just standard wear and tear.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: But spot that shadow in the dead of night, and it could easily pass for some vengeful ghost hovering at your bedside... Haha, don't you think so?

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Now that we've confirmed there's nothing wrong here, let's move on to inspect the next area.

The real estate developer, having barely regained his composure, makes no effort to hide his impatience. Clearly unwilling to linger, he turns on his heel and marches out, leaving you and Luminita trailing a step behind.
Faint footsteps echo from the corner. You turn around—in the dim light, what appears to be a shadowy figure quickly slips around the turn.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Chief, wrong turn. We need to go this way.
I know, but I thought I saw something over there...

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Hmm? What did you see?
You look back toward the corner, only to find it completely empty now. Nothing is there except a ceiling light buzzing with poor electrical contact.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Your eyes must be playing tricks on you. Don't go scaring yourself!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: We still have another floor to check. Faster we move, faster we're out. Chief, if you're really that scared, just stick close and don't fall behind.
Before you can respond, she grabs your sleeve and practically drags you in the opposite direction, as if even one second lingering near that corner might cause her to work overtime.

Her sudden urgency leaves you bewildered. You stumble forward from the force of her pull, instinctively trying to look back. But before you can fully turn your head, you feel another sharp tug on your sleeve.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: But our progress today has been much faster than I expected! At this rate, once those rumors are cleared up, this place should be ready for demolition soon, right?
Based on what we've seen so far, that should be the case, as long as nothing unusual comes up.
You seem quite concerned about the demolition?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Of course! I won't get the final payment for this commission until the demolition officially begins.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Besides, I'm sure the Bureau wants this demolition over with too, right?
You don't immediately answer Luminita's question.

Despite obvious signs suggesting the real estate developer's shady dealings with the demolition, this technically falls outside the Bureau's jurisdiction. And given how deteriorated these buildings are, swift demolition is probably the right call.
With no Mania residue found here and these "hauntings" debunked, the Bureau has no reason to oppose the demolition project moving forward.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Yeah, you have no reason to oppose it.
She nods, naturally equating you with the Bureau, seemingly confirming something to herself through this classification. You sense something off in her tone and are about to press further...

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: How much longer do you two plan to waste time over there?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Coming! Sorry for the hold-up—right behind you!
Luminita trots quickly after him, her face instantly resuming its standard radiant smile. That thoughtful expression from moments ago seems almost like it was just your imagination.

The rest of the inspection unfolds without a hitch, with Luminita effortlessly debunking every supposedly paranormal incident you encounter. Slowly, the real estate developer's tense posture relax, his initial unease giving way to relief.
Maybe trying to salvage his pride after his earlier jumpy display, the developer grows much more talkative, venting his emotions and no longer concealing his true opinions about the old district.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: I knew it! There's no such thing as ghosts in this world, and even if there were, what are the odds they'd all haunt MY turf? Now it's time to squeeze those holdouts and find out who's been feeding these rumors.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Their greed just never ends. Holding out for more money, then pulling this crap? Guess they don't even want the pittance we're offering anymore...
Just as you turn into a corridor, before the real estate developer can complete his sentence, a precariously dangling light bulb above suddenly plummets to the ground, shattering into pieces.
Then comes the second bulb, the third, continuing all the way to the end of the corridor. Darkness surges in like a flood, engulfing your entire field of vision within seconds.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: How many times is this going to happen? The same old trick again. Miss Luminita, I suppose this is another case of unstable voltage, right?

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: ...Miss Luminita?
The expected reply never comes, leaving only complete silence surrounding you. You turn around.
Luminita is gone.
Bang!

All the open doors throughout the building suddenly slam shut in unison, the rotten floor beneath your feet shuddering upon the tremendous noise. Footsteps, alternating between light and heavy, materialize out of thin air. In the pitch-black darkness, shadowy figures seem to dart past, their shrill laughter echoing around you.

The darkness heightens your senses, making everything around you feel contaminated with dread. A sharp ringing fills your ears as your heart pounds like a drumbeat echoing throughout your body. A chill slowly creeps up your spine.

But what troubles you even more is that since these disturbances began, the shackles connecting you to Luminita have grown extremely weak. This usually indicates the safety of the Sinner is threatened—not a good sign at all.
This realization overrides your instinctive fear. You need to find her quickly. As you prepare to move, a hand suddenly grabs the hem of your coat with desperate strength.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Oh no... there really are ghosts... Hey! Where are you going?

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: You do know what you're doing, right? Just get me out of here first! Once we're safe, I'll pay you however much you want!
My responsibility to the Sinner comes first. I need to check on Luminita's condition.

The Bureau has already screened this place for Corruptor risks, and I haven't detected any abnormal Mania fluctuations. If you're afraid to leave on your own, find a safe spot and wait for me to return.

You shake off his grip, but barely take a step before his hand clamps around your arm again. From the cracked walls comes a shrill, skittering laughter—mocking your struggle, sending a chill down your spine.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Don't push it! You brought this Sinner here, and now she's run off because she clearly knew there was something wrong with this place. When they start looking for someone to blame, you'll also be in line!

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Should've known better than to trust some two-bit agent. Takes the money and can't even do the job right! **** it...
His barrage of offensive words shows no signs of abating. You have borne this man's shameless behavior for far too long, reaching the limits of your tolerance.
You know exactly how this demolition project really works, and who'll take the fall when it's over.
I don't have time for this. Let go!

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: You... Ouch!
Exhausted by his shameless arguments, you use a swift, practiced movement to break free from his grip and immediately head deeper into the corridor.

Within moments, the developer's footsteps echo behind you. You have no energy to worry about him now as you focus all your attention on the fragile shackle connection, trying to pinpoint Luminita's exact location.

The aged floorboards groan under your weight as indistinct laughter and whispers echo through the air. You feel your way forward in the darkness, unable to see clearly, but you sense something lurking in the shadows, its gaze fixed on your back.
The shackles lead you to a narrow door at the far end of the corridor. Without hesitation, you slam it open.
Luminita!
You can hardly call this a room. It's cramped, disordered, and crammed with dust-covered, decrepit furniture.
Luminita lies collapsed in the center, surrounded by grimy couches with stuffing protruding out. She shows no response to your call, appearing completely unconscious.
Other sounds emerge in the room, twisting and crawling along the walls and floor, breaking intermittently as they echo around you.
Home... is gone... what now...
...Why... did you take... my... our...
You pay no heed to the raspy whispers that surround you and instead rush forward to check on Luminita.
But in the next instant, something seizes your ankle. You instinctively whirl around to look.

Before you can make out its form, the massive dark shadow instantly constricts your limbs, then your neck, mouth, and nose, gradually robbing you of breath and consciousness. You hear the anguished cries of the real estate developer, who is also succumbing to the same mysterious assault.
The shackles within your body pulse in response to Mania. A Corruptor? No—you recognize this power all too well.

You grab at the thing coiled around your neck. As you release your shackles, darkness engulfs your vision. Simultaneously, a flood of foreign memories floods your consciousness, infiltrating your mind through the connection of the shackles.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: My, where have you been wandering to come home so late? Go wash up, dinner's ready.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I wasn't wandering! Just... fell asleep on the bus and missed my stop...

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Grandma, listen! Those demolition people came again. They were handing out stuff in the neighborhood and told me to bring one home for the adults.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: Let me check... Oh, this? Just put it with the old newspapers. I already signed a demolition contract.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: Lumy, we'll be moving to a new home soon.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Huh? But didn't everyone say those people were scammers who just wanted to steal our homes?

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: That was before they changed management. The new developer's made it clear to us. This demolition is a government decision meant to improve people's living conditions.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: This contract's got all the proper stamps, the compensation money will come right to us on time, and our new home will have better conditions and location than here. They've even got night buses there, so you can play outside till the stars come out and still get back safe...

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: Goodness, why am I explaining grown-up things to you? Off to wash those hands now—your dinner's going cold!

Bam. Bam. Bam. The hammering at their door shattered the quiet of their home. Before they could react, strangers poured inside—shouting, shoving, and smacking an official demolition permit onto the table before the grandmother and granddaughter.

steps.speaker: Demolition Staff A
steps.content: Stop wasting time. You're holding up our work. Pack up and get out now.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: This wasn't our agreement... The relocation date hasn't even come. This is against the law. I will report you!

steps.speaker: Demolition Staff B
steps.content: Your "relocation date" means nothing. Demolition day is today. That contract's signed, stamped, and legally binding—go cry to a judge. Should've read the fine print, grandma. Only person to blame is you.

steps.speaker: Demolition Staff B
steps.content: You've got half a day to pack. Once the machines start rolling, we won't be liable if your brittle old bones get crushed!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Mister, my grandma's really old... M-my parents usually deal with this stuff, but they're away working. So we don't really understand all this...

steps.speaker: Demolition Staff A
steps.content: You think the kid's telling the truth? If the property's really under the parents' names, this could get messy, and that's not the kind of report management wants to hear.

steps.speaker: Demolition Staff B
steps.content: Truth my ***! Two people live here—that's it. Last time we fell for the "helpless kid" act, but this little schemer's full of tricks. Probably learned it all from the old hag.

steps.speaker: Demolition Staff B
steps.content: Get out of the way, now!

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: She's just a child, she doesn't understand... Please, we'll go—we'll go right now. Lumy, sweetheart, hold Grandma's hand...

Her grandmother had never taught her such lies. But at that moment, the old woman said nothing—only gripped her granddaughter's fingers and placed her own frail body between the child and those intimidating men.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Grandma... I wasn't smart enough. What do we do now...?

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: Oh, don't cry, sweetheart. None of this is your fault. Grandma will find us a new place to stay... Here, Lumy, help me read this address. These old eyes aren't as sharp as they once were. Ah, I really am old...

steps.speaker: Landlord A
steps.content: No, absolutely not. An old woman and a kid living off a pension? Can you even pay rent on time? Look, don't waste your breath. I'm not running a charity here. No means no.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Agent
steps.content: To be frank, with your... situation, options are limited. But there are workarounds—if you're willing to cover some "extra fees." Standard rates won't apply here. I'm sure you get what I mean.

steps.speaker: Landlord B
steps.content: You need to be out by next week at the latest! Clear out quickly. I have urgent plans for this place.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: Could you possibly give us a few more days? Next week is far too soon, cough cough... We won't have enough time to find another place.

steps.speaker: Landlord B
steps.content: Not my problem. That's just how things are. If you don't own property in Eastside, you'd better get used to situations like this.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Excuse me! Please wait.
Late at night in their rented room, the gravely ill elderly woman couldn't stop coughing. Luminita brought her warm water and painkillers with practiced ease, all traces of her past panic gone.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Don't worry, Grandma. I've kept copies of our lease agreement and all the bills. I talked to the landlord—she can't just break the contract and throw us out without a reason.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: According to the agreement, we can stay for another month. Before then, I'll definitely find...

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: Lumy, my child, it's all my fault. I'm so sorry.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: No, Grandma, this is not your fault.
Her denial never reached her grandmother's heart. The old woman just muttered weakly, her clouded eyes glued to the ceiling, drowning in guilt and worry.

steps.speaker: Grandmother
steps.content: A house is what makes a home, and now our home... is gone... Oh, Lumy, how will you manage now?
Home... is gone...

The Mania fluctuations are suppressed by the shackles. The voice that was echoing throughout the room suddenly becomes clearer, blending with the old woman's words from the memory, prompting you to react swiftly.
You pull off the thing wrapped around your body—a pitch-black curtain. From below comes the clinking of a chain, Luminita's weapon of choice, the other end firmly gripped in her hand.

steps.speaker: Young Boy
steps.content: Luminita, are you okay?

A child crouches beside Luminita, whose face has drained of color, anxiously checking on her. Behind him, there's a hole in the floor—and beside the tiles, a tape recorder whirs, endlessly looping the whispers that had filled the room.

steps.speaker: Young Boy
steps.content: Stay back! I'm not going to let you hurt Luminita!

The real estate developer lies unconscious on the floor nearby. Fortunately, he's only fainted from fright and has no visible injuries. After confirming the situation is under control, you turn your attention back to the wary child standing protectively in front of Luminita.
You're one of the residents' children, aren't you? Are you creating these hauntings to stop the old district from being demolished?

steps.speaker: Young Boy
steps.content: I-I don't know what you're talking about.
The boy's denial comes out shrill, unnatural. His eyes lock onto yours—too wide, unblinking—as if sheer intensity could force you to believe him.
His behavior says enough, especially paired with everything else you've noticed: darting shadows, the prickle of unseen eyes, and voices and footsteps that seem to follow you from every direction...
If none of this is actually caused by Mania, then everything is just like the tape recorder on the floor...
...the kind of "ghost-staging tricks" Luminita has mentioned.
Are there other children in the building?

steps.speaker: Young Boy
steps.content: No...
For a "haunting" this elaborate, there must be more people involved than just you. Did Luminita put you all up to this?

steps.speaker: Young Boy
steps.content: It wasn't Luminita's fault! It was our idea, she was just trying to help us!

steps.speaker: Young Boy
steps.content: Those mean people started it first. They kicked us out, even though this is our home...

The child doesn't get to finish—Luminita's hand yanks him behind her for protection. She staggers upright, breath ragged, but it's not the shackles weighing her down. Her current weakened state seems more like she has been attacked by something.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Cough... When did you figure it out?
I got suspicious after meeting the developer. Then I noticed people still in the building, and you kept changing the subject while probing my stance on the demolition—that's when I knew.
But I never imagined you'd go as far as faking an attack, even using your power on yourself just to sell the act and leaving yourself this vulnerable.
You were trying to make it look like a Corruptor attack, weren't you? I must say, you really went above and beyond for authenticity.
Toward the end, your composure cracks. Luminita tilts her head in confusion, as if not understanding why you are upset, before her practiced smile slides back into place.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Right, I should've known. Once the Bureau and you got involved, I was bound to get caught.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Okay, sure, our haunted property adventure might've had some... coordination difficulties. But come on—you've got to admit the overall atmosphere was pretty impressive. Told you we didn't need real ghosts with me in the lead!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Besides, I didn't even charge you, Chief, so cut me some slack, alright? Who knew that developer would chicken out that hard?
Luminita, are you seriously going to keep avoiding the issue with this act?
At this point, no one's going to buy the "just a prank" excuse anymore.

Your words echo through the silent room. She watches you quietly, the smile on her lips gradually flattening into a straight line. The silence between you stretches like an over-tightened string, ready to snap at any moment.
The next second, a soft scoff breaks the standoff.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: ...You're right. Keeping up this charade wouldn't look good on me, and it's pointless anyway.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Look, that jerk down there and those backing him stole the relocation funds meant for the residents in the old district. Now that they can't cover up their embezzlement, they're turning the screws on the property owners here instead.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Those contracts are nothing but legal traps—no provision for relocation housing, no demolition compensation. The residents tried to hold them off by refusing to sign, but I never imagined they'd stoop this low.
So you worked with the property owners to spread haunting rumors, all to delay the demolition project?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: If we could scare you officials today, that would be ideal. But even if that failed, just spreading rumors about "Corruptor sightings causing fainting spells in the old district" would've stalled demolition anyway.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: How's that for an answer? Does that satisfy your curiosity, Chief?
You ignore the mockery and hostility in her words and continue your questioning.
Why continue with this plan even after coming to the Bureau? You had other options.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Of course I knew it was risky and wouldn't solve the root problem. But it would at least save the houses and buy them time.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: As long as these houses are still standing, people have something to fight for, a chance to find a real solution...
You know that's not what I'm asking.
Luminita is stunned for a few seconds. After making out your expression, she finally grasps your words left unsaid. Then she lets out a soft laugh, as if she's heard something amusing.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: You're asking why I didn't just come clean during my interrogation and seek help from you and the Bureau, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: But why should I trust you?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: You've never opposed the higher-ups' decision to demolish the old district, and you've admitted that the developers are difficult to deal with. Officially, you're a Bureau employee—practically in the same boat as them.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Even official documents with signatures and seals can be elaborate traps. And I'm just a dangerous Sinner under your supervision, Chief. I have no reason whatsoever to believe you'd actually help me.

Her voice stays detached, as if she's merely stating objective facts. The recorder on the floor continues to whisper about "home" over and over, unexpectedly bringing to mind the bedridden elder and the child staying at her bedside.
If you really thought we were on opposite sides, weren't you worried I'd hold you accountable once everything came out?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: The haunting rumors were entirely my idea. I couldn't just watch the old district get trampled, so I stuck my nose where it didn't belong. I'm just not good enough to scare you off.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: If you're not convinced and send investigators anyway, they'll confirm the property owners "knew nothing about it," and these children were just manipulated by me.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Of course, after today, there might be fresh rumors about monsters appearing in the old district and someone fainting. How many would believe it? What impact would they have? Well, that would have nothing to do with "me."
Just then, your comms device suddenly springs to life with an alert.
The atmosphere in the room instantly freezes. Luminita clearly isn't as confident as she's been pretending to be—you notice her hand tightening once again on her end of the weapon.
In the silent standoff, you press the answer button on the device, never taking your eyes off Luminita's face.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, you've significantly exceeded your scheduled return time. I've noticed that both you and Sinner Luminita are still located in the old district. Is there a problem?
We encountered Corruptors that broke in unexpectedly. The developer fainted from shock, and several children are trapped here. No other casualties. Please help send backup.
Also, please notify the relevant departments that all demolition activities in this area must be suspended. I'll explain the details when I return.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Understood. Medical team and backup are on their way.
You end the call, and silence reclaims the room.
Luminita's face is hidden in the shadow of her beret, only her exceptionally bright eyes visible, staring at you in disbelief.
